class line_width                                                        
    {                                                                 
    public:                                                           
                                                                      
        line_width(int value)                                               
            : m_value(value)                                          
        {                                                             
            id();                                                     
        }                                                             
        static int id()                                               
        {                                                             
            static int id = std::ios_base::xalloc();                  
            return id;                                                
        }                                                             
        int value() const                                             
        {                                                             
            return m_value;                                           
        }                                                             
                                                                      
    private:                                                          
                                                                      
        int m_value;                                                  
    };                                                                
                                                                      
    inline std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& out, const line_width& n) 
    {                                                                 
        out.iword(line_width::id()) = n.value();                            
        return out;                                                   
    }
objects.description: Iostream manipulator class to set per-stream line width for pretty-printing. Stores an int and writes it into the stream’s iword slot identified by id().

Internal helper struct representing a loaded NumPy .npy file. Users must ensure types and layout match or exceptions are thrown.

functions.name: xt::argument
functions.signature:
template <std::size_t I, class... Args>
constexpr decltype(auto) xt::argument(Args&&... args) noexcept
functions.description: Returns the I-th argument from a parameter pack, perfectly forwarded. Useful for forwarding arguments by index without creating a tuple.
requirements: I must be less than sizeof...(Args); otherwise a static_assert fails.
Args... can be any types; the I-th argument must be valid to return by forwarding reference.
Noexcept by design; does not throw.

functions.name: xt::apply
functions.signature:
template <class R, class F, class... S>
R xt::apply(std::size_t index, F&& func, const std::tuple<S...>& s) NOEXCEPT(noexcept(func(std::get<0>(s))))
functions.description: Invokes func on the tuple element at runtime position index and returns the result converted to R. This provides a runtime switch over a tuple’s alternatives.
requirements: index must be in the range [0, sizeof...(S)); passing an out-of-range index results in undefined behavior (array index out of bounds).
func must be callable as func(std::get<I>(s)) for the selected I and the returned value must be convertible to R.
The noexcept condition depends on calling func on the first tuple element; mismatched noexcept may affect exception specifications.

functions.name: xt::nested_copy
functions.signature:
template <class T, class S>
void xt::nested_copy(T&& iter, const S& s)
functions.description: Writes a scalar value into the output sequence via an output iterator, then advances the iterator. Intended to be the base case for copying from nested initializer_lists into a flat destination.
requirements: iter must be a valid output iterator whose value_type is assignable from S.
Dereferencing iter and incrementing it must be valid operations.

functions.name: xt::resize_container
functions.signature:
template <class C>
bool xt::resize_container(C& c, typename C::size_type size)
functions.description: Resizes a generic container c to the given size using c.resize(size). Returns true to indicate the resize was performed.
requirements: C must provide a resize(typename C::size_type) member function.
The requested size must be within any constraints of C; otherwise c.resize may throw or have container-defined effects.

functions.name: xt::resize_container
functions.signature:
template <class T, std::size_t N>
bool xt::resize_container(std::array<T, N>& a, typename std::array<T, N>::size_type size)
functions.description: Checks whether a std::array can match the requested size. Returns true if size equals N, otherwise false; std::array has fixed size and is not modified.
requirements: No resize is performed; callers should check the boolean return and handle false appropriately.
size must equal N to return true.

functions.name: xt::resize_container
functions.signature:
template <std::size_t... I>
bool xt::resize_container(xt::fixed_shape<I...>& a, std::size_t size)
functions.description: Checks whether a fixed_shape matches the requested size. Returns true if size equals the rank (number of template indices), otherwise false.
requirements: The size parameter must equal sizeof...(I) to return true.
No mutation is performed; callers should check the boolean return.

functions.name: xt::normalize_axis
functions.signature: std::size_t xt::normalize_axis(std::size_t dim, std::ptrdiff_t axis)
functions.description: Normalizes a possibly negative axis index with respect to a dimensionality dim. Negative axes are converted by adding dim; non-negative axes are returned unchanged.
requirements: If axis is negative, dim + axis must be non-negative; callers must ensure the resulting index is in [0, dim).
No bounds check is performed; callers should validate the result is < dim if required.

functions.name: xt::normalize_axis
functions.signature:
template <class E, class C>
std::enable_if_t<!xtl::is_integral<std::decay_t<C>>::value && xtl::is_signed<typename std::decay_t<C>::value_type>::value, xt::rebind_container_t<std::size_t, std::decay_t<C>>> xt::normalize_axis(E& expr, C&& axes)
functions.description: Normalizes a container of signed axis indices against expr.dimension(). Negative axes are wrapped by adding the dimension. Returns a new container with std::size_t indices and asserts that all are within bounds.
requirements: C must be a non-integral container with a signed value_type; it must support size(), operator[], begin(), end(), and be rebindable to std::size_t via rebind_container.
expr must provide dimension() and support use in the bound checks.
Each axes[i] should be in [-expr.dimension(), expr.dimension()-1] so that the normalized value is in [0, expr.dimension()).
Assertions (XTENSOR_ASSERT) will fail in debug if any normalized axis is out of range.

functions.name: xt::normalize_axis
functions.signature:
template <class C, class E>
std::enable_if_t<!xtl::is_integral<std::decay_t<C>>::value && std::is_unsigned<typename std::decay_t<C>::value_type>::value, C&&> xt::normalize_axis(E& expr, C&& axes)
functions.description: Validates and forwards a container of unsigned axis indices. No normalization is needed; asserts that all axes are within [0, expr.dimension()). Returns the original container by forwarding.
requirements: C must be a non-integral container with an unsigned value_type; it must support begin() and end().
expr must provide dimension().
All axis values must be < expr.dimension(); otherwise XTENSOR_ASSERT may fail in debug builds.

functions.name: xt::forward_normalize
functions.signature:
template <class R, class E, class C>
auto xt::forward_normalize(E& expr, C&& axes) -> std::enable_if_t<xtl::is_signed<std::decay_t<decltype(*std::begin(axes))>>::value, R>
functions.description: Normalizes a range of signed axis indices and returns them in a container of type R. Elements are converted using normalize_axis(expr.dimension(), ax). Asserts that the resulting axes are in range.

R must be default-constructible and resizable via xt::resize_container(R&, size_t).

functions.name: xt::make_overlapping_memory_checker
functions.signature:

functions.name: xt::throw_broadcast_error
functions.signature:
template <class S1, class S2>
[[noreturn]] void xt::throw_broadcast_error(const S1& lhs, const S2& rhs);
functions.description: Always throws a broadcast_error describing incompatible array dimensions. In debug builds, the message includes the left-hand-side and right-hand-side shapes by iterating their elements; in non-debug builds, it throws a generic message. Intended to be called when shape broadcasting fails.
requirements: This function never returns; callers must not assume normal control flow continues.

functions.description: Always throws a concatenate_error indicating incompatible array dimensions for concatenation. In debug builds, the error message includes both shapes by iterating their elements; in non-debug builds, it throws a generic message.
requirements: This function never returns; callers must not assume normal control flow continues.
S1 and S2 must be shape-like types that are iterable with cbegin()/cend() and whose value_type can be streamed to std::ostream (only required in debug builds where detailed messages are constructed).

functions.name: xt::check_index
functions.signature:
template <class S>
void xt::check_index(const S& shape);
functions.description: No-op overload used when no indices are provided. Exists to terminate variadic recursion for index checking.
requirements: No requirements; does not perform any checks.
S may be any type; it is unused in this overload.

functions.name: xt::check_element_index
functions.signature:
template <class S, class It>
void xt::check_element_index(const S& shape, It first, It last);
functions.description: Checks that a contiguous sequence of element-wise indices fits within the leading axes of shape. It aligns the checked portion to the last min(shape.size(), distance) indices of [first,last). Throws std::out_of_range if any checked index j for axis k satisfies j >= shape[k] and shape[k] != 1 (size-1 axes are permissive for broadcasting).
requirements: S must provide size() and operator[] to access axis extents.
Iterator It must be a random-access iterator; the implementation uses last - first and pointer arithmetic.
The iterator's value_type must be comparable with the axis sizes; it is cast/compared against values of S.
The function throws std::out_of_range on invalid indices; callers should handle this exception.

functions.name: xt::check_dimension
functions.signature:
template <class S, class... Args>
void xt::check_dimension(const S& shape, Args...);
functions.description: Verifies that the number of supplied indices does not exceed the number of dimensions of shape. Throws std::out_of_range if sizeof...(Args) > shape.size().
requirements: S must provide size() returning the rank (number of dimensions).
This function only checks the count of indices, not their values.
On violation, throws std::out_of_range; callers should handle this exception.

functions.name: xt::check_axis_in_dim
functions.signature:
template <class A, class D>
void xt::check_axis_in_dim(A axis, D dim, const char* subject = "Axis");
functions.description: Validates that an axis index lies within [-dim, dim-1]. Negative axes are supported (Python-style). Throws std::out_of_range with a message prefixed by subject when out of range.
requirements: dim must represent the total number of dimensions; it is compared as both unsigned and signed (internally cast to std::make_signed_t<D>).
axis may be negative; it must satisfy -dim <= axis < dim.
On violation, throws std::out_of_range; callers should handle this exception.
subject is an optional C-string used in the error message; it must be a valid null-terminated string if provided.

functions.name: xt::check_access
functions.signature:
template <class S, class... Args>
void xt::check_access(const S& shape, Args... args);
functions.description: Convenience function that combines check_dimension and check_index to validate both the arity and bounds of a set of indices against shape. Throws on the first violation encountered.
requirements: All requirements of xt::check_dimension and xt::check_index apply.
On violation, throws std::out_of_range; callers should handle this exception.

template <class T = void, class E, class X, class EVS = DEFAULT_STRATEGY_REDUCERS, XTL_REQUIRES(std::negation<is_reducer_options<X>>)> 
inline auto xt::nanmean(E&& e, X&& axes, EVS es = EVS())
functions.description: Mean excluding NaNs along specified axes: nansum(...) divided by count of non-NaN elements.
requirements: axes must be valid for e.
Weights not used; types chosen to avoid precision loss when T=void.

functions.name: xt::nanvar
functions.signature:
template <class T = void, class E, class EVS = DEFAULT_STRATEGY_REDUCERS, XTL_REQUIRES(is_reducer_options<EVS>)>
inline auto xt::nanvar(E&& e, EVS es = EVS())
functions.description: Variance excluding NaNs over all elements; computed as nanmean((x - nanmean(x))^2).

functions.name: xt::nanstd
functions.signature:
template <class T = void, class E, class EVS = DEFAULT_STRATEGY_REDUCERS, XTL_REQUIRES(is_reducer_options<EVS>)>
inline auto xt::nanstd(E&& e, EVS es = EVS())
functions.description: Standard deviation excluding NaNs over all elements; sqrt(nanvar(e)).

functions.name: xt::diff
functions.signature:
template <class T>
auto xt::diff(const xexpression<T>& a, std::size_t n = 1, std::ptrdiff_t axis = -1)
functions.description: Compute the n-th discrete difference along the given axis. Not lazy: returns a concrete container. For boolean data, computes inequality (difference) as not_equal.
requirements: axis is normalized to a valid axis of a; negative axis selects from end.
If n > size along axis, the result has size 0 along that axis.
n may be 0 to return input as-is.

functions.name: xt::trapz
functions.signature:
template <class T>
auto xt::trapz(const xexpression<T>& y, double dx = 1.0, std::ptrdiff_t axis = -1)
functions.description: Integrate y along axis using the composite trapezoidal rule with constant spacing dx. Returns a realized array (not lazy).
requirements: axis must be valid for y.
dx is spacing between samples; must make sense for the units used.

functions.name: xt::interp
functions.signature:
template <class E1, class E2, class E3, typename T>
inline auto xt::interp(const E1& x, const E2& xp, const E3& fp, T left, T right)
functions.description: One-dimensional piecewise linear interpolation of (xp, fp) evaluated at x. Values left of xp[0] get 'left'; values right of xp[-1] get 'right'. Returns a 1D xtensor with same length as x.
requirements: xp must be 1D and sorted ascending (asserted).
x must be sorted ascending (asserted).
fp must have same length as xp.

functions.name: xt::unwrap
functions.signature:
template <class E1, class E2 = xt::placeholders::xtuph, class E3 = double>
inline auto xt::unwrap(E1&& p, E2 discontinuity = xnone(), std::ptrdiff_t axis = -1, E3 period = 2.0 * xt::numeric_constants<double>::PI)
functions.description: Unwrap a sequence by correcting jumps larger than discontinuity with respect to a given period (default 2π). If discontinuity placeholder is used, defaults to period/2. Handles boundary ambiguities for floating types.
requirements: axis must be valid for p.
If discontinuity is placeholder, it becomes period/2; otherwise values below period/2 are treated as period/2; use discontinuity > period/2 to change behavior.
period defines wrapping range; type-dependent ambiguity handling is applied.

functions.name: xt::cov
functions.signature:
template <class E1>
inline auto xt::cov(const E1& x, const E1& y = E1())
functions.description: Compute covariance matrix. If only x is provided: for 1D x returns 1x1 variance; for 2D x (shape [m, n]) returns m×m covariance across the second axis (columns). If y is provided (1D), stacks x and y then computes covariance.
requirements: If y is provided and not empty, it must be one-dimensional and compatible for stacking with x.
For 2D x, expects x.dimension()==2; asserts otherwise.
Divides by (N-1) where N is number of samples along the variable axis; assumes N>1.

functions.name: xt::convolve
functions.signature:
template <class E1, class E2, class E3>
inline auto xt::convolve(E1&& a, E2&& v, E3 mode)
functions.description: Compute 1D convolution of two 1D expressions a and v using the specified mode tag (convolve_mode::valid or convolve_mode::full). If v is longer than a, arguments are swapped for efficiency. Returns a realized 1D xtensor.
requirements: Both a and v must be 1D (checked; throws runtime_error on invalid dimensions).
Both inputs must have size > 0 (asserted).
mode must be a tag type: convolve_mode::valid or convolve_mode::full.

constexpr R xt::get_strides(const xt::fixed_shape<X...>& shape) noexcept
functions.description: Computes compile-time strides for a fixed_shape under the given layout (row_major or column_major). Returns the strides container R with zeros for dimensions of size 1. Intended for fixed-size tensors where shape is encoded in the type.
requirements: L must be xt::layout_type::row_major or xt::layout_type::column_major (other layouts are not supported).
R must be a strides-like container constructible from a braced initializer list of ptrdiff_t-sized values and sized to match the rank of the fixed shape.

Function is noexcept and must not throw.

functions.name: xt::get_backstrides
functions.signature:
template <class S, class T>
constexpr T xt::get_backstrides(const S& shape, const T& strides) noexcept
functions.description: Computes backstrides from a shape and strides: backstrides[i] = strides[i] * (shape[i] - 1). Useful for bounded iteration across fixed or dynamic tensors.
requirements: shape and strides must have the same rank/size.
Elements of shape must be >= 1 for meaningful backstrides; if shape[i] == 0 the expression (shape[i] - 1) underflows for unsigned shapes (caller responsibility).
T must be constructible from a braced initializer list of the computed values and indexable.
Function is noexcept and must not throw.

functions.name: xt::xstrided_view::store_simd
functions.signature:
template <class CT, class S, xt::layout_type L, class FST>
template <class align, class simd, class T /*= xexpression_type*/>
auto xt::xstrided_view<CT, S, L, FST>::store_simd(size_type i, const simd& e) -> enable_simd_interface<T, void>
functions.description: Store a SIMD vector e into the underlying storage at position i with alignment policy align. Enabled only when the underlying expression supports SIMD and the view layout is not dynamic.
requirements: Participates only if has_simd_interface<T>::value is true and L != layout_type::dynamic.
i must be within the underlying storage bounds for this view.
The provided align tag must be compatible with the storage alignment; misaligned access behavior depends on the chosen align mode (driven by align and data_alignment).
simd must be a SIMD value type supported by xt_simd::store_as.

functions.name: xt::xstrided_view::build_view
functions.signature:
template <class CT, class S, xt::layout_type L, class FST>

auto xt::xstrided_view<CT, S, L, FST>::build_view(E&& e) const -> rebind_t<E>
functions.description: Rebind this view's shape/strides and offset to a different underlying expression e, producing a new xstrided_view with the same geometry and layout.
requirements: E must be bindable (closure) to the view's FST::rebind_t<E> flat storage getter.

functions.name: xt::strided_view
functions.signature:
template <xt::layout_type L = xt::layout_type::dynamic, class E, class S, class X>
auto xt::strided_view(E&& e, S&& shape, X&& strides, std::size_t offset = 0, xt::layout_type layout = L) noexcept
functions.description: Free function to build a strided view from an expression, explicit shape, strides, and offset. Returns an xt::xstrided_view with static layout L (or dynamic).
requirements: shape and strides must have the same dimensionality.
offset must not cause out-of-bounds access when combined with the view size.
layout must be a valid xt::layout_type.
E must be an xtensor-compatible xexpression; returned view references e's storage.

functions.name: xt::reshape_view
functions.signature:
template <xt::layout_type L = XTENSOR_DEFAULT_TRAVERSAL, class E, class S>
auto xt::reshape_view(E&& e, S&& shape)
functions.description: Create a view that reinterprets e's data with a new shape in traversal order L. If shape is a signed container and contains a single -1, that dimension is inferred so that the total size matches e.size().
requirements: L must be xt::layout_type::row_major or xt::layout_type::column_major (enforced by static_assert).
If shape's value_type is signed, it may contain at most one -1 (asserted).
If shape has no -1 (or is unsigned), the product of its dimensions must equal e.size() (inferred/assumed; one dimension may be recalculated only for signed shapes with -1).

functions.name: xt::sort
functions.signature:
template <class E>
inline auto xt::sort(const xexpression<E>& e, placeholders::xtuph /*t*/)
functions.description: Returns a flattened, sorted copy of the input xexpression. Uses std::sort on a temporary contiguous buffer and returns a 1-D container of the same value_type. Intended for callers passing xnone() to indicate flattening.
requirements: e must be a valid xt::xexpression with random-access iteration; it will be evaluated (copied) before sorting.
Element type of e must be strictly weak-order comparable with operator< (required by std::sort).
Result is a new container; original input is not modified.

functions.name: xt::argsort
functions.signature:
template <class E>
inline auto xt::argsort(const xexpression<E>& e, placeholders::xtuph /*t*/, sorting_method method = sorting_method::quick)
functions.description: Returns the indices that would sort the flattened input. Produces a 1-D index container aligned with the flattened data. Uses either std::sort (quick) or std::stable_sort (stable) on the index array with a comparator into the data.
requirements: e must be a valid xt::xexpression with random-access iteration; data are read-only.
method selects the indirect sorting algorithm: quick (no stability guarantee) or stable (preserves order of equal elements).
Element type must be comparable with operator< unless a custom comparator is supplied internally (default is operator<).
Returns a new index container of size e.size().

functions.name: xt::partition
functions.signature:
template <class E, class C, class R = detail::flatten_sort_result_type_t<E>, class = std::enable_if_t<!xtl::is_integral<C>::value, int>>
inline R xt::partition(const xexpression<E>& e, C kth_container, placeholders::xtuph /*ax*/)
functions.description: Flattens the input and partially sorts it in-place in a copy so that all provided k-th positions contain the elements that would be at those positions in a fully sorted order. Elements before each k are less-or-equal and after are greater-or-equal, but the regions are unsorted. Returns the flattened partially sorted copy.
requirements: e is evaluated; the operation is performed on a temporary copy.
C must be a random-access container of index values (e.g., std::vector<std::size_t>, std::array<...>) and not an integral type.
kth_container's values must be valid indices in [0, e.size()-1].
Container is sorted internally; caller does not need to pre-sort.
Element type must be comparable with operator< (used by std::nth_element).

functions.name: xt::argpartition
functions.signature:
template <class E, class C, class R = typename detail::linear_argsort_result_type<typename detail::sort_eval_type<E>::type>::type, class = std::enable_if_t<!xtl::is_integral<C>::value, int>>
inline R xt::argpartition(const xexpression<E>& e, C kth_container, placeholders::xtuph)
functions.description: Flattens input and returns indices that would partition the array at the specified k-th positions. The returned 1-D index array has the property that when applied to e, each k-th element is in its final sorted position; elements on either side are unordered.
requirements: C must be a random-access container of indices (not an integral type).
Each index in kth_container must be in [0, e.size()-1].
e is read-only; only indices are produced.
Element type must be comparable with operator< (for indirect comparisons).

functions.name: xt::quantile
functions.signature:
template <class T = double, class E, class P>
inline auto xt::quantile(E&& e, const P& probas, std::ptrdiff_t axis, T alpha, T beta)
functions.description: Computes quantiles of e along the given axis for the probabilities in probas, using Hyndman and Fan’s parameterization with interpolation parameters alpha and beta. Internally performs partial sorting at interpolation indices and linearly interpolates adjacent order statistics. Returns an expression with a new leading axis for quantiles.
requirements: axis must be within [-e.dimension(), e.dimension()-1].
All entries of probas must satisfy 0 <= p <= 1 (asserted).
alpha and beta must be in [0, 1] (asserted).
Element type must support ordering and arithmetic used for interpolation.
e will be partially sorted on a copy along the axis; original is unchanged.

functions.name: xt::median
functions.signature:
template <class E>
inline typename std::decay_t<E>::value_type xt::median(E&& e)
functions.description: Computes the median of all elements in e as if flattened. Uses partition to place middle element(s) and averages the two middle values when the total count is even.
requirements: e.size() > 0 to be meaningful; for even sizes, value_type must support addition and division by 2.
Element type must be comparable with operator< (used by partition).

functions.name: xt::argmin
functions.signature:
template <layout_type L = XTENSOR_DEFAULT_TRAVERSAL, class E>
inline auto xt::argmin(const xexpression<E>& e)
functions.description: Returns the flat index (as a 0-D xtensor<size_t,0>) of the minimum element in e using the specified traversal layout.
requirements: e must be non-empty; std::min_element on an empty range is undefined.
E::value_type must be comparable with operator<.
L selects traversal order for iterators; use default unless specific layout is required.

functions.name: xt::argmax

inline auto xt::argmax(const xexpression<E>& e)

functions.name: xt::unique
functions.signature:
template <class E>
inline auto xt::unique(const xexpression<E>& e)
functions.description: Returns a 1-D xtensor of the sorted unique elements of e. Internally flattens, sorts, std::unique’s in place, and copies the unique range into a tightly-sized result.
requirements: Element type must be strictly weak-order comparable with operator< and equality comparable with operator== (used by std::unique).
Input is not modified; sorting occurs on a temporary copy.

functions.name: xt::setdiff1d
functions.signature:
template <class E1, class E2>
inline auto xt::setdiff1d(const xexpression<E1>& ar1, const xexpression<E2>& ar2)
functions.description: Computes the sorted set difference of unique values in ar1 not present in ar2. Returns a 1-D xtensor of values in unique(ar1) that are not in unique(ar2).
requirements: Element type of E1/E2 must be comparable with operator< and equality comparable (for unique and set_difference).
Both inputs are read-only; temporaries are created for unique and intermediate buffers.

functions.name: xt::random::get_default_random_engine

functions.name: xt::random::shuffle
functions.signature:
template <class T, class E = xt::random::default_engine_type>
void xt::random::shuffle(xexpression<T>& e, E& engine = xt::random::get_default_random_engine());
functions.description: In-place shuffle of elements along the first axis of an xcontainer. For 1-D, shuffles elements; for higher dimensions, permutes sub-arrays along axis 0. Uses Fisher–Yates with the provided engine.
requirements: Input must be an xcontainer/xexpression; function operates on e.derived_cast().

For ND, expects view(de, i) to be valid for 0 <= i < shape[0].

functions.name: xt::pad
functions.signature:
template <class E, class S = typename std::decay_t<E>::size_type, class V = typename std::decay_t<E>::value_type>
inline auto xt::pad(E&& e,
                    const std::vector<std::vector<S>>& pad_width,
                    xt::pad_mode mode = xt::pad_mode::constant,
                    V constant_value = 0)
functions.description: Pads an N-dimensional xtensor/xexpression by the specified before/after counts per axis. Returns a newly allocated array (temporary_type_t<E>) with the original data centered and borders filled according to mode: constant (fill with constant_value), symmetric (mirror around edge), reflect (mirror excluding edge), wrap/periodic (circular), or edge (replicate edge values). Typical use: provide per-axis {{before, after}, ...} padding widths and choose a mode.
requirements: pad_width.size() must equal e.shape().size() (asserted).
For each axis, if mode is wrap or periodic, nb (pad_width[axis][0]) and ne (pad_width[axis][1]) must be <= e.shape(axis) (asserted).
For each axis, if mode is symmetric, nb and ne must be <= e.shape(axis) (asserted).
For each axis, if mode is reflect, nb and ne must be <= e.shape(axis) - 1 (asserted).
For mode edge, no additional size assertions are enforced by the code; edges are broadcast to fill the region.
pad_width entries are treated as counts; providing negative values will be cast to an unsigned size_type and is likely invalid; callers should provide non-negative counts (inferred).
E must be an xtensor/xexpression-like type supporting shape(), shape(axis), and compatible with xt::strided_view; the result type is an owning temporary.
constant_value is used only when mode == xt::pad_mode::constant.

functions.name: xt::pad
functions.signature:
template <class E, class S = typename std::decay_t<E>::size_type, class V = typename std::decay_t<E>::value_type>
inline auto xt::pad(E&& e,
                    const std::vector<S>& pad_width,
                    xt::pad_mode mode = xt::pad_mode::constant,
                    V constant_value = 0)
functions.description: Pads an array using a single {before, after} pair replicated across all axes. Internally expands to per-axis {{before, after}, ...} and delegates to the primary pad overload. Returns a newly allocated array.
requirements: pad_width must contain exactly two elements: {before, after} (required by construction, otherwise out-of-bounds access will occur).
All requirements of the primary overload apply per axis: size constraints on nb/ne depending on mode (wrap/periodic: <= dim; symmetric: <= dim; reflect: <= dim-1).
Provided counts should be non-negative (inferred).
E must be an xtensor/xexpression-like type compatible with xt::strided_view; result is an owning temporary.
constant_value is used only when mode == xt::pad_mode::constant.

functions.name: xt::pad

inline auto xt::pad(E&& e,
                    S pad_width,
                    xt::pad_mode mode = xt::pad_mode::constant,
                    V constant_value = 0)
functions.description: Pads an array by the same number of elements before and after along all axes. Equivalent to using {{pad_width, pad_width}, ...} for every axis. Returns a newly allocated array.
requirements: All requirements of the primary per-axis overload apply with nb = ne = pad_width for each axis: depending on mode, pad_width must satisfy per-axis bounds (wrap/periodic: <= dim; symmetric: <= dim; reflect: <= dim-1).

E must be an xtensor/xexpression-like type compatible with xt::strided_view; result is an owning temporary.

template <class F, class E, class R, XTL_REQUIRES(std::is_convertible<typename E::value_type, typename R::value_type>)>
inline void copy_to_reduced(F& /*f*/, const E& e, R& result)
functions.description: Copies elements from expression e into result when E::value_type is convertible to R::value_type. Iterates e in its layout order and std::copy-s into the contiguous memory of result.
requirements: E must expose layout(), template cbegin<layout_type>(), template cend<layout_type>(), and contiguous iteration in the chosen layout

functions.name: xt::reduce_immediate
functions.signature:
template <class F, class E, class X, class O>
inline auto reduce_immediate(F&& f, E&& e, X&& axes, O&& raw_options)
functions.description: Performs an immediate reduction of expression e along axes using reducer functors f (reduce, init, merge), returning a concrete result container. Computes the output shape, iterates e efficiently depending on strides/layout, reduces values, and applies an optional initial value via options.
requirements: axes must be sorted in strictly increasing order (std::less)
axes must not contain duplicates
Each axis index must be in [0, e.dimension()-1] when axes is non-empty; otherwise a runtime exception is thrown

F must be a 3-tuple-like of functors (reduce_functor_type, init_functor_type, merge_functor_type) accessible with xt::get<0/1/2> and callable as: result_type reduce(init(), expr_value) and result_type merge(result_type, result_type)
E must be an evaluated xexpression-like object supporting: shape(), dimension(), layout(), strides(), data(), storage().begin()/end(), cbegin/cend iterators in both row_major and column_major
Result container is resized to the computed reduced shape and uses e.layout()
If all axes are reduced, the algorithm uses std::accumulate over e.storage() starting from either init() or the provided initial option; otherwise it iterates blockwise based on strides
If an initial value option is present, it is merged into each result element at the end

functions.name: xt::dump_npy
functions.signature:
template <typename E>
inline void xt::dump_npy(const std::string& filename, const xexpression<E>& e)
functions.description: Writes an xtensor-compatible expression to a NumPy .npy file on disk. It evaluates the expression, determines the NumPy dtype from E::value_type, constructs a NumPy header (v1.0 or v2.0 depending on size), and writes the raw contiguous data in binary. Typical usage: provide a writable filename and any xexpression (e.g., xarray, xtensor, or a computed expression) whose value_type is supported.
requirements: filename must refer to a path that can be opened for binary writing; otherwise a std::runtime_error is thrown.

E::value_type must be one of the supported scalar types mapped by the implementation (float, double, long double, signed/unsigned integral types, bool, std::complex<float>, std::complex<double>, std::complex<long double>); unsupported types cause a std::runtime_error ("Type not known.").
The expression must be evaluatable via xt::eval and provide a contiguous data() buffer after evaluation; this is satisfied by standard xtensor expressions.
On I/O failure to open the file, the function throws std::runtime_error; callers should handle exceptions.

functions.name: xt::load_npy
functions.signature:
template <typename T, layout_type L = layout_type::dynamic>
inline auto xt::load_npy(std::istream& stream)
functions.description: Loads a NumPy .npy array from the given input stream and returns an xtensor-adapted container of type T with shape/strides inferred from the file. The function validates the NPY magic, reads header (v1.0 or v2.0), allocates a buffer, reads the data, and casts it to the requested element type and (optionally) layout.
requirements: stream must be readable and positioned at the start of a valid NumPy .npy file; otherwise std::runtime_error is thrown.
Only NPY format versions 1.0 and 2.0 are supported; other versions cause std::runtime_error ("unsupported file format version").
The header must contain keys 'descr', 'fortran_order', and 'shape' in that order and formatted as produced by NumPy/this writer; otherwise parsing throws std::runtime_error.
The dtype typestring must match the regex '([<>|])[ifucb](\d+)' (e.g., '<f8', '|b1'); otherwise std::runtime_error is thrown.

T must correspond exactly to the file's dtype; otherwise a std::runtime_error is thrown with a format mismatch message. Supported T are those mapped by the implementation (float, double, long double, signed/unsigned integral types, bool, std::complex<float>, std::complex<double>, std::complex<long double>).

If L is specified as layout_type::column_major or layout_type::row_major, it must match the file's fortran_order flag; otherwise std::runtime_error is thrown for layout mismatch. Using L=layout_type::dynamic imposes no layout constraint.
Callers should handle exceptions for I/O and format errors.

functions.description: Allocates and returns an xtensor<T, N, L> with uninitialized elements and the given std::array shape (rank N).
requirements: shape.size() == N defines the tensor rank.
Elements are uninitialized; the caller must assign before reading.
T must be suitable for storage in xtensor<T, N, L>.
ST extents must be convertible to the xtensor shape type.

functions.name: xt::empty
functions.signature: template <class T, layout_type L = XTENSOR_DEFAULT_LAYOUT, class I, std::size_t N> inline xtensor<T, N, L> xt::empty(const I (&shape)[N])
functions.description: Allocates and returns an xtensor<T, N, L> with uninitialized elements and the given C-style array shape of rank N.
requirements: shape is a C-style array of length N defining extents.
Elements are uninitialized; the caller must assign before reading.
T must be suitable for storage in xtensor<T, N, L>.
I extents must be convertible to the xtensor shape type.

functions.name: xt::empty
functions.signature: template <class T, layout_type L = XTENSOR_DEFAULT_LAYOUT, std::size_t... N> inline xtensor_fixed<T, fixed_shape<N...>, L> xt::empty(const fixed_shape<N...>&)
functions.description: Creates and returns an xtensor_fixed with compile-time fixed shape N... and uninitialized elements. The shape parameter is ignored, serving only to select the overload.
requirements: The template parameter pack N... encodes the fixed extents at compile time.
Elements are uninitialized; the caller must assign before reading.
T must be suitable for storage in xtensor_fixed<T, fixed_shape<N...>, L>.

functions.name: xt::empty_like
functions.signature: template <class E> inline auto xt::empty_like(const xexpression<E>& e)
functions.description: Allocates a concrete xcontainer (matching E’s value type and layout) with the same shape as e, with uninitialized elements.
requirements: e must model xexpression and provide shape(), value_type, and layout compatible with temporary_type_t<E>.
Result elements are uninitialized; the caller must assign before reading.

functions.name: xt::full_like
functions.signature: template <class E> inline auto xt::full_like(const xexpression<E>& e, typename E::value_type fill_value)
functions.description: Allocates a concrete xcontainer matching e’s type/layout/shape, and fills all elements with fill_value.
requirements: e must model xexpression and provide shape().
fill_value must be convertible to E::value_type.
Returns an allocated, filled container (not lazy).

functions.name: xt::zeros_like
functions.signature: template <class E> inline auto xt::zeros_like(const xexpression<E>& e)
functions.description: Allocates a concrete xcontainer matching e’s type/layout/shape and fills it with zero.
requirements: e must model xexpression and provide shape().
E::value_type must be constructible from 0.
Returns an allocated, filled container (not lazy).

functions.name: xt::ones_like
functions.signature: template <class E> inline auto xt::ones_like(const xexpression<E>& e)
functions.description: Allocates a concrete xcontainer matching e’s type/layout/shape and fills it with one.
requirements: e must model xexpression and provide shape().
E::value_type must be constructible from 1.
Returns an allocated, filled container (not lazy).

functions.name: xt::eye
functions.signature: template <class T = bool> inline auto xt::eye(const std::vector<std::size_t>& shape, int k = 0)
functions.description: Creates a lazy xgenerator of the given shape with ones on the diagonal offset by k and zeros elsewhere. Works for at least 2-D shapes; diagonal is determined using the last two indices.
requirements: shape.size() must be at least 2; the diagonal is defined over the last two axes.
T is the generated value_type and must be constructible from 0 and 1.
k offsets the diagonal: k > 0 upper, k < 0 lower.

functions.name: xt::eye
functions.signature: template <class T = bool> inline auto xt::eye(std::size_t n, int k = 0)
functions.description: Creates a lazy xgenerator for an n x n identity-like matrix (ones on the k-offset diagonal, zeros elsewhere).
requirements: n defines a square (n x n) 2-D shape.
T is the generated value_type and must be constructible from 0 and 1.
k offsets the diagonal: k > 0 upper, k < 0 lower.

functions.name: xt::arange
functions.signature: template <class T, class S = T> inline auto xt::arange(T start, T stop, S step = 1) noexcept
functions.description: Creates a lazy xgenerator producing values in [start, stop) with a fixed step. For floating-like steps, the last element may be adjusted depending on internal logic.
requirements: step must be non-zero (division by zero would occur in size computation).
T and S must support subtraction, addition, division, and multiplication used to compute shape and values.
For unsigned integral step, start < stop yields non-empty; for signed integral step, direction must match step sign to produce elements.

functions.name: xt::arange
functions.signature: template <class T> inline auto xt::arange(T stop) noexcept
functions.description: Creates a lazy xgenerator producing values in [0, stop) with step 1.
requirements: T must support construction from 0 and 1 and arithmetic for range generation.
Assumes step = 1; stop can be zero to produce an empty range.

functions.name: xt::linspace
functions.signature: template <class T> inline auto xt::linspace(T start, T stop, std::size_t num_samples = 50, bool endpoint = true) noexcept
functions.description: Creates a lazy xgenerator of num_samples values linearly spaced from start to stop. If endpoint is true, the last sample equals stop; otherwise it is excluded.
requirements: num_samples is the length of the generated 1-D expression (may be zero).
T must be arithmetic; computations use common_type<T, double>.
endpoint controls inclusion of stop; internal step uses fmax(1, num_samples - (endpoint ? 1 : 0)).

functions.name: xt::logspace
functions.signature: template <class T> inline auto xt::logspace(T start, T stop, std::size_t num_samples, T base = 10, bool endpoint = true) noexcept
functions.description: Creates a lazy xgenerator of num_samples values spaced evenly on a log scale: returns pow(base, linspace(start, stop, ...)).
requirements: num_samples defines output length.
T must be arithmetic; pow(base, value) must be defined for the promoted types in the xt context.
endpoint mirrors linspace semantics for including the final exponent.

functions.name: xt::xtuple
functions.signature: template <class... Types> inline auto xt::xtuple(Types&&... args)
functions.description: Creates a std::tuple whose element types are xtl::const_closure_type_t<Types>..., preserving const-closure semantics suitable for xt concatenation/stack helpers.
requirements: Arguments are perfectly forwarded; resulting tuple stores closures to the inputs.
Use as input to xt::concatenate/xt::stack variants expecting a tuple of xexpressions.

functions.name: xt::concatenate
functions.signature: template <class... CT> inline auto xt::concatenate(std::tuple<CT...>&& t, std::size_t axis = 0)
functions.description: Concatenates xexpressions along the specified axis, returning a lazy xgenerator that reads from the appropriate input based on the index.
requirements: All inputs in t must have the same dimension.
All shapes must match on every axis except the concatenation axis; sizes along the concatenation axis are summed.
axis must be a valid axis index (< dimension).
On mismatch, an exception is thrown via throw_concatenate_error.

functions.name: xt::concatenate
functions.signature: template <std::size_t axis, class... CT, typename = std::enable_if_t<detail::all_fixed_shapes<CT...>::value>> inline auto xt::concatenate(std::tuple<CT...>&& t)
functions.description: Concatenates fixed-shape xexpressions at compile time along the template axis, returning a lazy xgenerator with a fixed (compile-time) resulting shape.
requirements: All inputs must have fixed shapes (enforced by SFINAE).
All shapes must match on every axis except the concatenation axis; sizes along the concatenation axis are summed.
The template axis must be valid w.r.t. input ranks.

functions.name: xt::stack
functions.signature: template <class... CT> inline auto xt::stack(std::tuple<CT...>&& t, std::size_t axis = 0)
functions.description: Stacks xexpressions along a new axis (inserts a dimension of size equal to the number of inputs at the given axis), returning a lazy xgenerator.
requirements: All inputs should have identical shapes; stacking inserts a new axis of length sizeof...(CT).
axis is the insertion index into the result shape (0 <= axis <= input dimension).

functions.name: xt::hstack
functions.signature: template <class... CT> inline auto xt::hstack(std::tuple<CT...>&& t)
functions.description: Stacks xexpressions horizontally (column-wise): concatenates along axis 1 for arrays with dimension > 1, otherwise along axis 0 for 1-D inputs. Returns a lazy xgenerator.
requirements: All inputs should have compatible shapes for the chosen concatenation axis (match on all other axes).
Inputs of dimension 1 are treated as row vectors for axis selection.

functions.name: xt::vstack
functions.signature: template <class... CT> inline auto xt::vstack(std::tuple<CT...>&& t)
functions.description: Stacks xexpressions vertically (row-wise): effectively concatenates along the first axis; for 1-D inputs, shapes are treated as (1, N) before stacking. Returns a lazy xgenerator.
requirements: All inputs should have compatible shapes for concatenation along the first axis (match on other axes).
For 1-D inputs, they are treated as shape (1, N) during stacking.

functions.name: xt::meshgrid
functions.signature: template <class... E> inline auto xt::meshgrid(E&&... e) noexcept
functions.description: Returns a tuple of lazy xgenerators that broadcast/replicate the 1-D input coordinate arrays into coordinate grids suitable for vectorized evaluation over an N-D grid.
requirements: Each input e must be at least 1-D and provide shape()[0].
Inputs should represent 1-D coordinate vectors; lengths determine the grid sizes.

functions.name: xt::diagonal
functions.signature: template <class E> inline auto xt::diagonal(E&& arr, int offset = 0, std::size_t axis_1 = 0, std::size_t axis_2 = 1)
functions.description: Returns a lazy xexpression yielding the elements of arr along the diagonal defined by (axis_1, axis_2) with a given offset. For ndim > 2, other axes are preserved and the diagonal length is appended as the last dimension.
requirements: arr must have dimension >= 2.
axis_1 and axis_2 must be valid axis indices within arr.dimension() and can be equal only if such semantics are desired (typical use has axis_1 != axis_2).
offset may be positive or negative; diagonal size is adjusted accordingly.

functions.name: xt::diag
functions.signature: template <class E> inline auto xt::diag(E&& arr, int k = 0)
functions.description: Given a 1-D array, returns a lazy xexpression of shape (n+k_abs, n+k_abs) with arr placed on the k-offset diagonal and zeros elsewhere.
requirements: arr must be 1-D; n is arr.shape()[0].
k offsets the diagonal: positive shifts above, negative below the main diagonal.
E::value_type must be constructible from 0 for off-diagonal fill.

functions.name: xt::tril
functions.signature: template <class E> inline auto xt::tril(E&& arr, int k = 0)
functions.description: Returns a lazy xexpression with elements of arr below (and including) the k-offset diagonal preserved and zeros elsewhere (lower-triangular extraction).
requirements: arr must have dimension >= 2 (the comparison uses the first two indices).
k selects the diagonal: 0 main, k < 0 below, k > 0 above.
E::value_type must be constructible from 0 for masked elements.

functions.name: xt::triu
functions.signature: template <class E> inline auto xt::triu(E&& arr, int k = 0)
functions.description: Returns a lazy xexpression with elements of arr above (and including) the k-offset diagonal preserved and zeros elsewhere (upper-triangular extraction).
requirements: arr must have dimension >= 2 (the comparison uses the first two indices).
k selects the diagonal: 0 main, k < 0 below, k > 0 above.
E::value_type must be constructible from 0 for masked elements.

functions.name: xt::noalias_proxy::noalias_proxy
functions.signature:
template <class A>
xt::noalias_proxy<A>::noalias_proxy(A a) noexcept
functions.description: Constructs a noalias_proxy wrapping the target array/expression A. Intended to be created via xt::noalias(target) and then used on the left-hand side of assignments/compound-assignments to perform no-alias, in-place evaluation on the target.
requirements: Argument a must be a valid target object compatible with the proxy’s assignment/compound-assignment operations (i.e., it must provide the called assign/plus_assign/... members).
The wrapped target must remain valid for the lifetime of the proxy and during any subsequent operations performed through it.
Construction is noexcept per declaration.

functions.name: xt::noalias_proxy::operator=
functions.signature:
template <class A, class E>
disable_xexpression<E, A> xt::noalias_proxy<A>::operator=(const E& e)
functions.description: Assigns a scalar value e (i.e., not an xt::xexpression) to the proxied target without aliasing checks. Internally forwards to m_array.assign(xscalar<E>(e)). Use as xt::noalias(a) = scalar;
requirements: E must not be an xexpression type (enforced by disable_xexpression).
The wrapped A must support assign from xscalar<E>.
E must be convertible to the target’s value type for assignment.

functions.name: xt::noalias_proxy::operator+=
functions.signature:
template <class A, class E>
disable_xexpression<E, A> xt::noalias_proxy<A>::operator+=(const E& e)
functions.description: Performs in-place addition of a scalar e to the proxied target without aliasing checks, via m_array.scalar_computed_assign(e, std::plus<>()).
requirements: E must not be an xexpression type.
The wrapped A must implement scalar_computed_assign(value, std::plus<>()).
A’s value_type and E must be addable with std::plus<> (i.e., operator+ must be valid).

functions.name: xt::noalias_proxy::operator-=
functions.signature:
template <class A, class E>
disable_xexpression<E, A> xt::noalias_proxy<A>::operator-=(const E& e)
functions.description: Performs in-place subtraction of a scalar e from the proxied target without aliasing checks, via m_array.scalar_computed_assign(e, std::minus<>()).
requirements: E must not be an xexpression type.
The wrapped A must implement scalar_computed_assign(value, std::minus<>()).
A’s value_type and E must be subtractable with std::minus<> (i.e., operator- must be valid).

functions.name: xt::noalias_proxy::operator*=
functions.signature:
template <class A, class E>
disable_xexpression<E, A> xt::noalias_proxy<A>::operator*=(const E& e)
functions.description: Performs in-place multiplication of the proxied target by a scalar e without aliasing checks, via m_array.scalar_computed_assign(e, std::multiplies<>()).
requirements: E must not be an xexpression type.
The wrapped A must implement scalar_computed_assign(value, std::multiplies<>()).
A’s value_type and E must be multiplicatively compatible with std::multiplies<> (i.e., operator* must be valid).

functions.name: xt::noalias_proxy::operator/=
functions.signature:
template <class A, class E>
disable_xexpression<E, A> xt::noalias_proxy<A>::operator/=(const E& e)
functions.description: Performs in-place division of the proxied target by a scalar e without aliasing checks, via m_array.scalar_computed_assign(e, std::divides<>()).
requirements: E must not be an xexpression type.
The wrapped A must implement scalar_computed_assign(value, std::divides<>()).
Division between A’s value_type and E must be valid with std::divides<>; division by zero is undefined behavior for integral types.

functions.name: xt::noalias_proxy::operator%=
functions.signature:
template <class A, class E>
disable_xexpression<E, A> xt::noalias_proxy<A>::operator%=(const E& e)
functions.description: Performs in-place modulus of the proxied target by a scalar e without aliasing checks, via m_array.scalar_computed_assign(e, std::modulus<>()).
requirements: E must not be an xexpression type.
The wrapped A must implement scalar_computed_assign(value, std::modulus<>()).
A’s value_type and E must support modulus with std::modulus<> (typically integral types).
Behavior for zero modulus divisor follows the underlying type semantics (typically undefined).

disable_xexpression<E, A> xt::noalias_proxy<A>::operator&=(const E& e)
functions.description: Performs in-place bitwise AND of the proxied target with a scalar e without aliasing checks, via m_array.scalar_computed_assign(e, std::bit_and<>()).
requirements: E must not be an xexpression type.
The wrapped A must implement scalar_computed_assign(value, std::bit_and<>()).
A’s value_type and E must support bitwise AND (typically integral or bitmask-like types).

template <class A, class E>
disable_xexpression<E, A> xt::noalias_proxy<A>::operator|=(const E& e)
functions.description: Performs in-place bitwise OR of the proxied target with a scalar e without aliasing checks, via m_array.scalar_computed_assign(e, std::bit_or<>()).
requirements: E must not be an xexpression type.
The wrapped A must implement scalar_computed_assign(value, std::bit_or<>()).
A’s value_type and E must support bitwise OR (typically integral or bitmask-like types).

functions.signature:
template <class A, class E>
disable_xexpression<E, A> xt::noalias_proxy<A>::operator^=(const E& e)
functions.description: Performs in-place bitwise XOR of the proxied target with a scalar e without aliasing checks, via m_array.scalar_computed_assign(e, std::bit_xor<>()).
requirements: E must not be an xexpression type.
The wrapped A must implement scalar_computed_assign(value, std::bit_xor<>()).
A’s value_type and E must support bitwise XOR (typically integral or bitmask-like types).

functions.name: xt::noalias
functions.signature:
template <class A>
noalias_proxy<xtl::closure_type_t<A>> xt::noalias(A&& a) noexcept
functions.description: Factory function creating a noalias_proxy for a target array/expression a. Use on the left-hand side to perform no-alias assignments/compound-assignments, e.g., xt::noalias(a) = rhs;
requirements: Argument a must be a valid target for subsequent assignment/compound-assignment operations exposed by noalias_proxy (i.e., its closure_type must support those operations).

The returned proxy contains a closure_type_t<A>; the lifetime/ownership semantics follow xtl::closure_type_t (callers must ensure the underlying target outlives the proxy and any immediate operations).
Function is noexcept per declaration.

functions.name: xt::xvectorizer::operator()
functions.signature:
template <class... E>
xfunction_type<E...> operator()(E&&... e) const;
functions.description: Applies the stored scalar callable (held by xt::xvectorizer<F,R>) to the provided arguments in an element-wise, lazy fashion by constructing and returning an xt::xfunction over those arguments. Typical usage: obtain an xvectorizer via xt::vectorize and then call operator() with xtensor/xexpression arguments to get an xfunction that broadcasts/combines them element-wise using the underlying scalar function. Details about broadcasting and evaluation are handled by xt::xfunction and are not specified here.
requirements: The number of arguments E... must match the arity of the stored callable m_f.
Each argument E must be acceptable to xt::xclosure_t<E> and usable to construct xt::xfunction<F, xclosure_t<E>...> (i.e., the arguments should be valid xt expressions/closures).
The stored callable F must be invocable with the scalar value types corresponding to the provided arguments (after any implicit conversions performed by xfunction).
Arguments are perfectly forwarded; callers must ensure they do not pass dangling references or otherwise invalid temporaries for the intended lifetime of the resulting xfunction object.

Any shape/size/broadcast compatibility requirements are enforced by xt::xfunction and the provided arguments; incompatibilities will result in compile-time errors or runtime errors depending on xt::xfunction semantics, which are not defined in this header.

functions.name: xt::vectorize

template <class R, class... Args>
xvectorizer<R (*)(Args...), R> vectorize(R (*f)(Args...));
functions.description: Creates an xt::xvectorizer from a raw function pointer f with signature R(Args...). The resulting vectorizer adapts the scalar function into an element-wise operation over xt expressions, to be invoked later via operator() to produce an xt::xfunction.
requirements: Parameter f must be a non-null pointer to a function with signature R(Args...).
R and Args... must match the pointed-to function type; R is the scalar return type used by the vectorizer.
The pointed-to function must be callable for scalar values compatible with the element types of the arguments that will later be passed to the vectorizer.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: arbitrary string
# Generate diverse but valid byte buffers used as std::string contents.

MAX_SIZE = 4096

def _pattern_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    remain = n
    while remain > 0:
        choice = rng.randrange(6)
        chunk_len = min(remain, rng.randint(1, max(1, remain)))
        if choice == 0:
            # ASCII letters repeated
            ch = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters)
            s = ch.encode('ascii') * chunk_len
        elif choice == 1:
            # Digits and punctuation mix
            alphabet = (string.digits + "-_:. ,|/")
            s = bytearray(chunk_len)
            for i in range(chunk_len):
                s[i] = ord(rng.choice(alphabet))
            s = bytes(s)
        elif choice == 2:
            # Include zeros and small values pattern
            s = bytearray(chunk_len)
            for i in range(chunk_len):
                s[i] = rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 13, 0])
            s = bytes(s)
        elif choice == 3:
            # High bytes
            s = bytes(rng.randint(128, 255) for _ in range(chunk_len))
        elif choice == 4:
            # Sequential increasing bytes wrapping 0..255
            start = rng.randint(0, 255)
            s = bytes(((start + i) & 0xFF) for i in range(chunk_len))
        else:
            # Random bytes
            s = bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(chunk_len))
        parts.append(s)
        remain -= len(s)
    return b"".join(parts)

def _ensure_variety(b: bytearray, rng: random.Random) -> None:
    # Ensure at least one zero and one non-zero, and at least one high byte if possible.
    if len(b) == 0:
        return
    if 0 not in b:
        b[rng.randrange(len(b))] = 0
    if all(x == 0 for x in b):
        b[rng.randrange(len(b))] = 1
    if not any(x >= 128 for x in b):
        b[rng.randrange(len(b))] = 200

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a base length with bias towards smaller but sometimes larger sizes
    choices = [rng.randint(1, 64), rng.randint(65, 512), rng.randint(513, 2048)]
    length = min(rng.choice(choices), MAX_SIZE)

    # Build content in segments to mix patterns
    segs = rng.randint(2, 6)
    sizes = []
    remaining = length
    for i in range(segs):
        if i == segs - 1:
            sizes.append(remaining)
        else:
            # Leave space for remaining segments
            max_sz = max(1, remaining - (segs - 1 - i))
            sz = rng.randint(1, max_sz)
            sizes.append(sz)
            remaining -= sz

    buf_parts: List[bytes] = []
    for sz in sizes:
        if sz > 0:
            buf_parts.append(_pattern_bytes(rng, sz))
    buf = bytearray(b"".join(buf_parts))
    _ensure_variety(buf, rng)

    # Occasionally prepend or append structured tokens
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        tokens = [b"", b"::", b"\n", b"\x00", b"-", b" "]
        pre = rng.choice(tokens)
        post = rng.choice(tokens)
        buf = bytearray(pre) + buf + bytearray(post)
        if len(buf) > MAX_SIZE:
            buf = buf[:MAX_SIZE]

    if not buf:
        buf = bytearray(b"A")

    return bytes(buf)

import os
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target data type: filesystem path
# The fuzz stubs use FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME() to obtain a writable filename and then
# write/read NumPy .npy data. We should provide a bytes buffer that the fuzzer runtime
# will use to seed its file content generation and any FUZZ_PARAM accesses.
#
# Strategy:
# - Provide a self-contained valid .npy file payload for a small array of doubles
#   so that when the harness treats the FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME as an existing file,
#   opening/reading yields a valid NPY. Some fuzzers mirror the bytes into files.
# - Also include multiple valid NPY variants and benign random padding to explore
#   both v1.0 and v2.0 headers, different shapes (1D and 2D), row-major order,
#   and consistent typestring '<f8'.
# - Keep size <= 4096 bytes.
#
# We construct one NPY payload deterministically from seed, choosing 1D or 2D shape
# with total elements <= 128 (as in stubs) and doubles. We then concatenate two NPY
# payloads separated by some padding so either the first or second could be used
# by the environment as file content.


def _pad_to_16(n: int) -> int:
    return ((n + 15) // 16) * 16


def _npy_header_dict(shape: List[int], fortran: bool, descr: str) -> bytes:
    # Build the Python dict text exactly as NumPy v1/v2 writers do in xt::dump_npy:
    # {'descr': '<f8', 'fortran_order': False, 'shape': (3, 4), }
    shape_str = str(tuple(shape))
    # Ensure trailing comma for 1D/ND tuples
    if len(shape) == 1 and not shape_str.endswith(',)'):
        # Python prints (n,) for 1D
        shape_str = f"({shape[0]},)"
    items = [
        f"'descr': '{descr}'",
        f"'fortran_order': {str(fortran)}",
        f"'shape': {shape_str}",
    ]
    txt = '{' + ', '.join(items) + ', }'
    return txt.encode('latin1')


def _make_npy(seed: int, version: int, shape: List[int]) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Magic
    magic = b"\x93NUMPY"
    assert version in (1, 2)
    ver_major = version
    ver_minor = 0
    # dtype: little-endian float64
    descr = '<f8'
    fortran = False

    header_dict = _npy_header_dict(shape, fortran, descr)
    if version == 1:
        # v1.0: header_len is uint16, header must end at 16-byte alignment
        # header = magic + ver(2) + len(2) + header + padding\n
        # Compute padding so that len(magic+ver+len+header+pad) % 16 == 0
        # After magic(6) + ver(2) + len(2) = 10 bytes before header.
        pre = 10
        pad_len = (_pad_to_16(pre + len(header_dict) + 1) - (pre + len(header_dict) + 1))  # +1 for newline
        header = header_dict + b' ' * pad_len + b"\n"
        header_len = len(header)
        if header_len > 65535:
            # Fallback to v2 if too large (shouldn't happen with small shapes)
            return _make_npy(seed, 2, shape)
        header_len_packed = struct.pack('<H', header_len)
        prefix = magic + bytes([ver_major, ver_minor]) + header_len_packed
    else:
        # v2.0: header_len is uint32, alignment to 16 bytes with newline
        pre = 12  # magic(6) + ver(2) + len(4)
        pad_len = (_pad_to_16(pre + len(header_dict) + 1) - (pre + len(header_dict) + 1))
        header = header_dict + b' ' * pad_len + b"\n"
        header_len_packed = struct.pack('<I', len(header))
        prefix = magic + bytes([ver_major, ver_minor]) + header_len_packed

    # Data: row-major doubles, deterministic from seed
    total = 1
    for s in shape:
        total *= int(s)
    base = rng.uniform(-1000.0, 1000.0)
    step = rng.uniform(-1.0, 1.0)
    data = [base + i * step for i in range(total)]
    payload = struct.pack('<' + 'd' * total, *data)

    return prefix + header + payload


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose shapes mirroring the stub constraints
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # 1D up to 128
        n = rng.randint(1, 128)
        shape1 = [n]
    else:
        # 2D with product <= 128
        d0 = rng.randint(1, 32)
        d1 = rng.randint(1, 32)
        while d0 * d1 > 128:
            if d1 > 1:
                d1 -= 1
            else:
                d0 = max(1, d0 - 1)
        shape1 = [d0, d1]

    # Second payload: different version and different shape kind
    if len(shape1) == 1:
        # Make a 2D companion
        d0 = rng.randint(1, 32)
        d1 = rng.randint(1, 32)
        while d0 * d1 > 128:
            if d0 > 1:
                d0 -= 1
            else:
                d1 = max(1, d1 - 1)
        shape2 = [d0, d1]
    else:
        # Make a 1D companion
        shape2 = [rng.randint(1, 128)]

    npy1 = _make_npy(seed ^ 0xA5A5_5A5A, version=1, shape=shape1)
    npy2 = _make_npy(seed ^ 0x5AA5_A55A, version=2, shape=shape2)

    # Combine with benign padding to keep total size under 4096
    sep = b"\n" * rng.randint(1, 8) + b"# padding\n"
    out = npy1 + sep + npy2
    if len(out) > 4096:
        # Truncate padding if necessary
        out = out[:4096]
    return out

import struct
import random
import io

# Generate a valid NumPy .npy (v1.0) file buffer for a small double array
# to be consumed by fuzzer stubs that call FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME and then
# write/read through xt::dump_npy / xt::load_npy. Although the stubs
# themselves write a file before loading, providing a valid initial file
# lets the harness exercise the loader path immediately when it chooses
# to read first.
#
# We emit arrays of dtype '<f8' (little-endian float64), with either 1D or 2D
# shapes capped to 128 elements to keep total size small.

def _make_header(descr: str, fortran_order: bool, shape):
    # Build a Python dict-like header exactly as NumPy does for v1.0
    # Keys must be in order: 'descr', 'fortran_order', 'shape'
    # booleans are written as True/False (capitalized), strings in quotes,
    # shape as tuple, ensuring a trailing comma for 1D singleton case.
    shape_tuple = tuple(int(x) for x in shape)
    shape_str = str(shape_tuple)
    header_dict = {
        'descr': descr,
        'fortran_order': fortran_order,
        'shape': shape_tuple,
    }
    # Construct the exact textual dict with keys in order
    header = "{ 'descr': '%s', 'fortran_order': %s, 'shape': %s }" % (
        header_dict['descr'],
        'True' if header_dict['fortran_order'] else 'False',
        shape_str,
    )
    # NPY v1.0 header: magic, version (1,0), 2-byte little-endian header_len
    # Header must be padded with spaces to make the entire header section
    # (10 + 2 + header_len) so that the data starts at a 16-byte alignment.
    header_bytes = header.encode('latin1')
    magic = b"\x93NUMPY"
    version = b"\x01\x00"
    # Compute padded header length
    # total = len(magic)+len(version)+2 + header_len
    # data starts at 10 + 2 + header_len; must be divisible by 16
    # Pad with spaces and a trailing newline
    pad_len = 16 - ((len(magic) + len(version) + 2 + len(header_bytes) + 1) % 16)
    if pad_len == 16:
        pad_len = 0
    padded = header_bytes + (b' ' * pad_len) + b'\n'
    header_len = struct.pack('<H', len(padded))
    return magic + version + header_len + padded


def _generate_data(shape, fortran_order, seed):
    # Generate deterministic float64 data with an affine pattern
    # Ensure no NaNs/Infs. Fill in row-major; Fortran-order flag only
    # affects consumer strides, not raw data layout in NPY (NumPy stores
    # Fortran arrays as column-major contiguous data). For simplicity,
    # we keep fortran_order=False to match dump behavior; but if set True,
    # we still provide contiguous column-major order.
    total = 1
    for s in shape:
        total *= s
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    base = rnd.uniform(-1000.0, 1000.0)
    step = rnd.uniform(-1.0, 1.0) or 0.5
    data = [base + i * step for i in range(total)]
    return struct.pack('<' + 'd' * total, *data)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    make_2d = rnd.choice([True, False])
    # dimensions 1..32; cap elements to <=128
    d0 = rnd.randrange(1, 33)
    d1 = rnd.randrange(1, 33)
    if make_2d:
        # shrink to keep product <= 128
        while d0 * d1 > 128:
            if d1 > 1:
                d1 -= 1
            else:
                d0 = max(1, 128 // d1)
                break
        shape = (d0, d1)
    else:
        d0 = min(d0, 128)
        shape = (d0,)

    # Match stubs: use row-major (fortran_order=False) and descr '<f8'
    descr = '<f8'
    fortran_order = False
    header = _make_header(descr, fortran_order, shape)
    data = _generate_data(shape, fortran_order, seed)
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    buf.write(header)
    buf.write(data)
    out = buf.getvalue()
    # Safety cap
    return out[:4096]
